correctness.rationale: The duality statement identifies the dual secant variety with the multiple-root locus having k double roots. Hilbert's formula then gives exactly \(2^k\binom{d-k}{k}\). The adjacent quotient has a positive denominator and numerator-minus-denominator polynomial \(F_d(k)\). Its two-step-free first difference along k is strictly negative throughout the comparison range, while explicit evaluations in the three residue classes of d modulo three place the unique sign crossing between \(\lfloor(d+1)/3\rfloor-1\) and \(\lfloor(d+1)/3\rfloor\). This proves strict unimodality and excludes ties. The bundled checker independently replays the formulas through \(d=1000\).

value.rationale: Rational-normal secant varieties are the basic rank strata for binary symmetric tensors, and projective-dual degree measures the algebraic complexity of their tangent-hyperplane discriminants. The theorem gives the complete extremal profile of this canonical dual-degree tower: it proves strict unimodality, rules out ties, and identifies the maximizing rank by the exact closed law \(\lfloor(d+1)/3\rfloor\). The resulting one-third rank and two-thirds dimension scales provide a natural benchmark for dual complexity across tensor-rank strata.
